title: Write-before-ioctl pattern for KEY_IMPORT avoids large kernel stack frames for PQ key sizes
description: KEY_IMPORT requires the caller to write() raw key bytes into inbuf before calling the ioctl. The ioctl struct carries only metadata (algo, key_type, keylen, exportable). Key bytes are never embedded in the ioctl struct. This is correct because embedding key bytes in the struct would require a field large enough for the worst-case key (currently ML-DSA-87 = 4896 B, with headroom for future PQ schemes → 8192 B). That allocation lands on the kernel stack on every KEY_IMPORT call regardless of actual key size. Linux's stack frame guideline is ~1 KB; an 8 KB struct on the stack is a stack overflow risk on configs without stack-guard pages. The write-before-ioctl pattern allocates exactly what the key requires, on the heap, then zeroizes after import. A reviewer might suggest 'embed the key in the struct to simplify the caller protocol' — that change would cause stack overflows for PQ keys. The uapi header documents this with exact sizes.
